title: Assignment 15 · Commercial context and past dealings
summary: Commercial context and past dealings. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Frigaliment Importing Co. v. B.N.S. International Sales Corp.: The buyer failed to prove that “chicken” in these contracts meant only young broilers rather than also including stewing hens.

Hurst v. W.J. Lake & Co.: A trade practice for rounding protein measurements could explain a contract requiring at least 50 percent protein, despite the apparent precision of the written number.

Nanakuli Paving & Rock Co. v. Shell Oil Co.: The jury could find that established price protection qualified Shell’s posted-price term and that imposing a sudden increase violated commercial standards of good faith.

Figgie International, Inc. v. Destileria Serralles, Inc.: Uncontradicted evidence of industry practice supplied an exclusive repair, replacement, or refund remedy; the completed refund prevented that remedy from failing merely because earlier repair efforts had been unsuccessful.

Columbia Nitrogen Corp. v. Royster Co.: A detailed written sales contract did not justify excluding trade-usage and prior-dealing evidence without asking whether that evidence could reasonably explain or supplement its terms.

Additional assigned materials: Restatement §§ 20, 200–204; UCC §§ 1-303, 2-202.
